inputs.root_cause: Applied the same fresh-literal-audit discipline that closed ORA-STREAM-001 earlier this session to NRRD-ARRAY-001's two obligations (SAL-NRRD-OBL-E4B3D1A206784660, SAL-NRRD-OBL-FEF73EC95DF631C3), whose own disclosed missing_behavior (a numpy/pynrrd adapter) was already confirmed NOT actually required by either obligation's own rule_text. Re-read array_view.py's own docstring claim ('Slicing, .transpose()/.permute(), .flip() and .crop() are all zero-copy') against the actual test file line by line and found slicing/crop/flip each have a direct `.data is view.data` identity proof, but transpose/permute do not -- an explicit clause of SAL-NRRD-OBL-FEF73EC95DF631C3's own rule_text ('zero-copy views where safe, explicit copies otherwise') left unproven for one of its four named operations.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-NRRD-OBL-E4B3D1A206784660 and SAL-NRRD-OBL-FEF73EC95DF631C3 (both NRRD-ARRAY-001) -- both promoted from partial to implemented after closing the last unproven per-operation clause.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Read array_view.py's own transpose() implementation directly before writing any test: `replace(self, shape=..., strides=..., axes=..., copied=False)` never includes `data` in its override set, so dataclasses.replace necessarily keeps the SAME `data` tuple reference from `self` -- confirming the implementation was already correct, and this was a testing gap, not a behavior gap. Added test_transpose_is_zero_copy_sharing_the_same_backing_data, mirroring the exact style and rigor of the existing test_slicing_is_zero_copy_sharing_the_same_backing_data/test_crop_selects_the_declared_sub_region/test_flip_reverses_axis_order_of_values proofs (`.data is view.data` identity assertion plus `.copied is False`). Also strengthened test_permute_is_an_alias_for_transpose_taking_one_sequence, which previously checked only `.shape` equality between `.permute()` and `.transpose()`, to additionally check `.strides`, `.axes` equality, and `.data is view.data` -- proving `.permute()` is a genuine full proxy for `.transpose()`, not merely shape-equivalent by coincidence.

execution_steps: 1. After committing and eventing ORA-STREAM-001's closure (FF6-EVENT-000487), pulled the full rule_text/required_tests/release_gates for nrrd's 6 remaining unresolved obligations directly from plans/strategic/ff6/obligations/nrrd.yaml (the authoritative source), then cross-referenced each against its own current missing_behavior in the implementation-evidence file.

2. Identified NRRD-ARRAY-001's own two obligations as the most promising target: both obligations' own sole disclosed remaining item (a numpy/pynrrd adapter) was ALREADY explicitly confirmed in a prior tick's own evidence text to not be required by either obligation's own literal rule_text -- meaning if that confirmation holds and nothing else is missing, these obligations could already be eligible for promotion, pending a fresh audit to confirm.

3. Read array_view.py's own full source (494 lines) end to end, comparing every operation's own implementation against both obligations' combined rule_text clauses: shape, strides, dtype, slicing, permutation, flip, crop, element access, orientation/per-axis-metadata propagation, and 'zero-copy views where safe, explicit copies otherwise'.

4. Cross-referenced every clause against the existing test file (test_obligation_array_view.py, 31 tests before this tick) to find which, if any, lacked a direct, literal proof rather than an inferred one -- found that slicing, crop, and flip each had their own explicit `.data is view.data` identity assertion, but transpose (and its .permute() alias) did not, despite the module's own docstring claiming all four operations are zero-copy.

5. Read transpose()'s own implementation directly to confirm the claim was actually true in behavior before writing any test: `replace(self, shape=..., strides=..., axes=..., copied=False)` never overrides `data`, so the same tuple object is necessarily retained -- this is a testing gap, not a behavior gap.
6. Added one new test (test_transpose_is_zero_copy_sharing_the_same_backing_data) matching the exact style and assertion pattern of the three existing sibling proofs.

7. Strengthened the existing, under-specified permute alias test to also verify strides/axes equality and zero-copy identity, not merely shape equality, since a permute() that happened to match transpose()'s shape by coincidence would not actually prove it is a correct, full alias.
8. Ran the full array-view test file (32 tests, up from 31) -- all passed on the first run, confirming the implementation needed no source change.
9. Ran ruff check on the changed test file: clean. No production source file was modified, so no mypy re-run against source code was needed.
10. Ran the full nrrd suite (958 passed, up from 957) and the 6-format FF6 regression (4358 passed, 4 skipped, up from 4357) -- exact +1 delta in both, confirming zero regressions.

11. Ran the installed-wheel proof (tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format nrrd, 1/1 PASS) as a sanity check confirming the package still builds and installs cleanly, even though no production source changed.
